candidates.name: app-store-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Node.js MIT-licensed module scraping the iTunes/Mac App Store: app details, ratings (overall + histogram), reviews (recency/helpfulness, up to 10 pages), search, developer app lists, curated collections, related apps. 164 commits, no committed data — a live client, not a dataset. Could pull Airbnb's current App Store rating/review-count/rank-in-collection on a schedule, but has no historical data itself.
candidates.why_useful: Addresses gap 5 (engagement: app rankings/reviews) and gap 14 (app-store review scrapers) as a acquisition method for point-in-time snapshots of ABNB's App Store standing; would need to be run repeatedly by us to build a time series, and per repo rules that scraping decision is left to a human.
candidates.last_activity: active fork lineage, exact last-commit date not surfaced by fetch
candidates.size_hint: code repo only, no data files

candidates.name: google-play-scraper (Node.js)
candidates.what_it_holds: Node.js MIT module extracting Google Play app details, ratings/reviews (with timestamps), install-count min/max estimates, category/genre metadata, similar apps, data-safety info. 496 commits; author states it is no longer actively maintained beyond community PRs. No committed data.
candidates.why_useful: Same use case as app-store-scraper but for Android: could snapshot Airbnb's Play Store install-count band, rating, and review volume as an engagement proxy (gap 5). No rank-chart data directly.

candidates.name: google-play-scraper (Python)
candidates.what_it_holds: Pure-Python, no-dependency MIT client for Google Play: app details, install counts, ratings/reviews (with continuation-token pagination), permissions, search. 187 commits.
candidates.why_useful: Python-native alternative to the Node scraper for the same engagement-snapshot use case (gap 5); easier to slot into this repo's pandas/duckdb pipeline than the Node tools.

candidates.name: appstorecat
candidates.what_it_holds: Self-hosted, open-source (MIT) 'app intelligence toolkit' with a Docker/MySQL/Redis stack. Explicitly does per-app 'App rankings' with 'per-app pivot across countries x collections x categories' and 'daily snapshots of top free/paid/grossing' for both App Store and Google Play, plus keyword density and locale-change tracking. 227 commits, 39 stars. No data committed to the repo itself — you self-host and it accumulates history in your own DB going forward.
candidates.why_useful: Closest thing found to a genuine rank-HISTORY tool: if stood up now it would start building a daily top-charts + per-app rank time series for Airbnb's travel-category rank on both stores, directly targeting gap 5's 'app downloads/rankings history'. It only starts collecting once deployed — no backfill of past ranks.
candidates.time_coverage: prospective only from time of deployment; no historical backfill
candidates.last_activity: recent (227 commits, small but apparently active project)
candidates.size_hint: application code, self-hosted DB not included

candidates.name: Google-Playstore-Dataset
candidates.what_it_holds: GitHub backup of a Kaggle dataset: 2.3 million Google Play apps x 24 attributes (installs band, rating, rating count, price, category, developer, size, content rating, etc.), collected June 2021, stored as split Part*.csv files to be reassembled; MIT license. Primary/updated copy lives on Kaggle at kaggle.com/gauthamp10/google-playstore-apps (which the author says receives newer refreshes than the GitHub mirror).
candidates.why_useful: A full-market snapshot that would include Airbnb's Play Store install-band/rating/review-count as of mid-2021; if multiple dated Kaggle versions of this dataset exist they could be strung into a coarse multi-year install-band/rating panel (gap 5). Single GitHub snapshot alone is not a time series.
candidates.time_coverage: June 2021 snapshot (GitHub copy); Kaggle host may have later versions
candidates.last_activity: static since ~2021 on GitHub; Kaggle side reportedly updated
candidates.size_hint: 2.3M rows, multi-part CSV, likely several hundred MB uncompressed

candidates.name: apple-appstore-apps
candidates.what_it_holds: GitHub backup of a Kaggle dataset: ~1.2 million iOS apps x 21 attributes (rating, price, developer, version, genre, etc.), collected October 2021 via Scrapy on cloud VMs, CC BY 4.0 licensed. Kaggle host: kaggle.com/gauthamp10/apple-appstore-apps.
candidates.why_useful: Companion iOS-side snapshot to the Play Store dataset above; would carry Airbnb's App Store rating/review-count metadata as of Oct 2021 for a historical anchor point (gap 5).

candidates.name: Appfigures CLI / MCP server
candidates.what_it_holds: Official Appfigures CLI and MCP server for querying the Appfigures paid API (app rank history, review data, revenue estimates, ad intelligence) from the terminal or an LLM agent.
candidates.why_useful: Would be the highest-fidelity route to real historical App Store/Play Store rank curves for Airbnb, but Appfigures requires a paid API key/subscription — out of bounds under this repo's 'never use paid API keys' rule. Catalogued only as a method for a human to consider licensing later.

candidates.name: appfigures_api (unofficial Python client, WIP)
candidates.what_it_holds: Work-in-progress unofficial Python wrapper for the Appfigures REST API.
candidates.why_useful: Alternative unofficial client to the official CLI; same paid-API-key limitation applies, and it is explicitly WIP/incomplete.

candidates.name: ex_figures
candidates.what_it_holds: Elixir wrapper for the Appfigures API.
candidates.why_useful: Same paid-API constraint as above; only relevant if the team later licenses Appfigures and happens to use Elixir. Low practical value now.

candidates.name: data-scrape/google-play-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Another Google Play scraping tool advertised as extracting app information, ratings, reviews, and 'rankings data' specifically (one of the few descriptions that explicitly claims ranking extraction, not just app metadata).
candidates.why_useful: If it genuinely exposes category rank (not just installs/ratings) it would be more directly useful for gap 5 than the more common metadata-only scrapers; worth a closer look/verification before use.

candidates.name: MrAdex77/google-play-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Node.js/TypeScript Google Play scraper explicitly listing 'top charts' among its supported endpoints, alongside app details, search, reviews, permissions, and data-safety info.
candidates.why_useful: One of the few scrapers that explicitly names top-charts retrieval, which is the closest proxy to a rank signal for Android; still a live-only client with no stored history, would need to be run on a schedule to build a series.
candidates.license: not individually confirmed (typically MIT for this genre)

candidates.name: playhound
candidates.what_it_holds: Unofficial Rust library for Google Play data extraction (app metadata, presumably ratings/reviews similar to the JS/Python equivalents).
candidates.why_useful: Marginal — a Rust-language alternative client with no unique data access advantage found over the more established JS/Python scrapers.

candidates.name: cmmntlnd
candidates.what_it_holds: Real-time monitor for App Store & Google Play reviews that forwards new reviews to Slack; a live alerting tool rather than a historical archive.
candidates.why_useful: Could be adapted to log every new Airbnb app review (with timestamp/rating) going forward into a running review-count/sentiment time series, addressing gap 14's review-scraper angle, but builds no history retroactively.

candidates.name: freshactors-scrapers
candidates.what_it_holds: Collection of Apify-based 'always fresh' scrapers spanning App Store, Google Play, Redfin, and Shopify App Store.
candidates.why_useful: Multi-target scraper suite; the App Store/Google Play actors could be pointed at Airbnb's listing for periodic metadata pulls, and the Redfin actor is tangential to gap 13 (housing). Runs on Apify's paid platform in practice, so mainly a method reference.

notes: This session's shared WebSearch budget (200/200) was already exhausted by other scouts before this theme's searches ran, so this pass was done entirely via WebFetch against github.com/topics pages, individual repo pages, and search-engine result pages (Google/Bing/DuckDuckGo fetches were mostly blocked by CAPTCHA or returned no extractable links; github.com/search itself hit HTTP 429 rate limiting twice and had to be avoided in favor of /topics/<tag> pages, which worked reliably). Coverage is therefore narrower than a full web-search pass would give. Clear finding: there is no free/open historical App Store or Google Play RANK-CHART time series on GitHub (no committed daily top-100 CSVs/JSON found, no dead-simple Wayback-Machine-of-app-charts repo). What exists instead are (a) live scraper/client libraries for both stores (app-store-scraper, google-play-scraper x2, several smaller forks) that could be run going forward to build our own series but hold no history themselves, (b) appstorecat, a genuinely rank-history-capable self-hosted toolkit that would need to be deployed now (no backfill), (c) two large one-time snapshot datasets (gauthamp10's Play Store and App Store dumps, 2021 vintage, GitHub-mirrored from Kaggle) that give a single historical anchor point for install-band/rating/review-count, and (d) Appfigures API clients (official + two unofficial), which are the correct tool for real rank history but are gated behind a paid subscription the repo rules disallow using. Sensor Tower and data.ai/App Annie have no open GitHub datasets or public-sample repos at all — every avenue tried (topics pages, profile search) came back empty. Recommend: if this gap matters enough to pursue, the actionable next step is deploying appstorecat or a scheduled run of one of the scraper libraries starting now (accepting no backfill), not further GitHub archaeology — the historical data simply is not sitting in a public repo anywhere found. A follow-up scout with a live WebSearch budget could still try Zenodo/Dataverse/HuggingFace directly (untried here beyond the blocked initial WebSearch calls) for an academic app-store-rank-history replication dataset, which is the one category this pass could not adequately check.
